questions.q: What are the four stages of hyperfocus?
a: Pick a task, cut distractions, focus, redirect
Plan the work, execute it, review it, rest
Breathe, stretch, write and repeat the cycle
Set a goal, time it, score it and share it
questions.why: Lesson 1 lists choosing one task, eliminating distractions, focusing and redirecting.

questions.q: How many things can your attention hold at once?
a: About 40
About 7
About 100
About 11 million
questions.why: Lesson 2 says you can process roughly 40 things at once, though short-term memory holds about seven.

Meditating for an hour each morning
Remembering everything you read
Ignoring your thoughts completely
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes it as looking outside your thoughts to see what has your attention.

questions.q: How can a timer help you stay focused?
a: It prompts you to check what has your attention
It forces you to finish the task faster
It blocks all websites automatically
It tracks how many hours you work
questions.why: Lesson 2 suggests an hourly timer as a cue to practice meta-awareness.

questions.q: What should you do if you must stay reachable while working?
a: Set specific times to check your phone
Keep the phone on the desk face up
Answer every message immediately
Turn off all notifications permanently
questions.why: Lesson 3 says to check your phone at set intervals and leave it alone in between.
